name: FastEmit: Low-latency Streaming ASR with Sequence-level Emission Regularization
problem: Streaming ASR emits words late because transducer training optimises full-sequence probability, not emission delay - and existing penalties need external alignments.
mechanism: Adds a sequence-level emission-latency regulariser directly to the transducer's per-sequence training objective, with no alignment information required. Because it regularises the sequence rather than individual token probabilities, it works across RNN-T, Transformer-T, ConvNet-T and Conformer-T without architecture changes.
speedup_reported: 150-300 ms latency reduction with significantly better accuracy than prior latency-reduction techniques (Early/Late Penalties, Constrained Alignments) on a Voice Search test set. Baseline methods are named and the test set identified, but hardware is not specified.
notes:
ICASSP 2021 per the arXiv comment. Mechanism relevance for inference: emission delay is a DECODING-SCHEDULING property, not a hardware one, so this class of fix is free at serving time once the model is trained with it. Contrast with the local-agreement approach used to retrofit streaming onto Whisper (pap record whisper-streaming): FastEmit bakes latency into training, Whisper-Streaming adds it at inference by re-running the encoder.
